Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: Digital authentication is fully functional via MauPass (launched December 2020) and the Mobile ID (launched September 2024). MauPass provides multi-level authentication (username/password; 2FA via SMS/email/KOREK app) using NIC-linked identity verified against the Central Population Database. The Mobile ID includes dual authentication and QR code verification. SAM card readers for chip-based authentication were also introduced under the Finance Act 2017.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Government portal authentication via NIC/MauPass is fully operational. MauPass is the single-window authentication platform for hundreds of government e-services, including MoKloud (digital safe), MRA (tax), PSC (job applications), Supreme Court portal, e-payslips, driving licence applications, motor vehicle licence payments, and appointment booking (MoRendezVous). Citizens register with their NIC number and the system validates against the Central Population Database.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Individuals can access their own data. The Data Protection Act 2017 grants data subjects the right to access, rectify, restrict, or erase personal data held by controllers. MauPass/MoKloud allows citizens to view their pre-populated civil data (name, address, NIC number). The Mobile ID allows citizens to view and manage their identity data via the MWA digital wallet app, including updating residential address and declaring lost cards. The DPA right of access is enforceable via the Data Protection Commissioner.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: KYC is fully enabled via the National Identity Card. The Bank of Mauritius, Civil Status Division, Mauritius Police Force and MTCI signed MOUs for a Central KYC database via InfoHighway. Banks (e.g. MauBank) require NIC for customer onboarding. ICTA SIM Registration Regulations 2023 mandate NIC for SIM registration KYC. Smile ID provides digital KYC verification using NIC. MauPass e-KYC uses Acuant to compare selfies against NIC document photo.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Comments: Judicial oversight with ID-specific mechanisms. The Supreme Court issued landmark rulings in 2015 (Madhewoo v. State; Jugnauth v. State) finding central biometric database storage unconstitutional, directly reshaping MNIC architecture. The UN Human Rights Committee ruled in 2021 that biometric storage on cards violated privacy. Section 2C of the NIC Act (inserted 2024) mandates independent security audits of the MNIC System. The Privy Council (Judicial Committee) also reviewed the MNIC case. ICT Appeal Tribunal handles DPA appeals.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Full integration. Mauritius has 100% civil registration coverage. A National Identity Number (NIN) is automatically computer-generated at birth registration (when at least one parent is Mauritian) and printed on the birth certificate. The same NIN is used on the national ID card at age 18, marriage certificates, and death deactivation — a complete lifecycle integration. The Civil Status Division manages both the CRVS and MNIC under the Prime Minister's Office, and data is shared via the Central Population Database and InfoHighway.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Fully available data sharing rules. The Data Protection Act 2017 (Section 3(4)(a)) permits inter-agency data exchange on a need-to-know basis. The Digital Government Transformation Strategy and National Open Data Policy formalise data reuse. The InfoHighway platform requires MOUs/application forms, High-Level Management Team approval (chaired by MTCI), and data encryption for all 169 inter-agency connections. The Central KYC initiative (Bank of Mauritius, Civil Status Division, Police, MTCI) further governs financial ID data sharing.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Digital ID-specific regulations exist. The NIC (Mobile ID) Regulations 2024 specifically govern the digital/mobile version of the identity card, including storage in digital wallets, authentication requirements, and permissible uses. These are the first regulations explicitly addressing a digital identity credential distinct from the physical card. The Finance Miscellaneous Provisions Act 2023 introduced the Mobile ID concept into law.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2017 (DPA 2017) came into force on 15 January 2018, repealing the 2004 Act. It aligns with EU GDPR principles, covers biometric data as a special category, mandates data controllers/processors to register, provides data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure), and requires 72-hour breach notification. Section 12 of the NIC Act explicitly subjects all MNIC data collection to the DPA.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Data Protection Office (DPO), headed by the Data Protection Commissioner, is the independent supervisory authority under the DPA 2017. It is under the aegis of the Ministry of Technology, Communication and Innovation but is fully independent operationally. It has powers to investigate complaints, conduct audits, issue enforcement notices, and oversee data protection compliance. The Data Protection Commissioner has publicly commented on compliance requirements for MNIC 3.0 and Mobile ID.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The National Identity Card (and Mobile ID) constitutes legal proof of identity. Section 7(2) of the NIC Act states: 'Where any person is required to produce evidence of his identity, it shall be sufficient for that purpose if he produces his identity card or Mobile ID.' The NIC is required for passport applications, voting, banking KYC, social security, SIM registration, and marriage publication.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Comprehensive legal framework exists. The National Identity Card Act (1985, as amended by Finance Act 2009, NIC Miscellaneous Provisions Act 2013, Finance Act 2017, Finance Miscellaneous Provisions Act 2023) governs the MNIC. In 2024 three new regulations were promulgated: NIC Regulations 2024, NIC (Card Usage) Regulations 2024, NIC (Mobile ID) Regulations 2024. The right to privacy is constitutionally entrenched.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: Partial in-country maintenance. MNIC 3.0 was developed in partnership with a Thales-led consortium (with Harel Mallac Technologies, a local firm). The National Identity Card Unit (under Prime Minister's Office) oversees day-to-day operations and policy. The original MNIC 2.0 was built under a Government-to-Government arrangement with Singapore (Singapore Cooperation Enterprise). Foreign vendors (Thales/Singapore) dominate technical development while Mauritian entities manage operations, indicating partial in-country maintenance.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Full Ministry of Finance oversight. The MNIC is funded via the national budget, with the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Acts (2009, 2017, 2023) being the primary legislative vehicle for MNIC amendments. Budget 2024-25 allocated resources for the new MNIC 3.0 system implementation. The CSD Annual Report 2023/24 reports MNIC revenue targets (Rs 17M estimated) as part of the national budget framework. The Ministry of Finance and Economic Development also sits on the High-Level Management Team for the InfoHighway data-sharing governance.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: Primarily domestic financing. The MNIC system is funded through the national government budget. While MNIC 3.0 was procured via contract with Thales/Harel Mallac (foreign/local consortium), the operational costs and ID issuance revenues are domestically funded. CSD Annual Report 2023/24 shows MNIC generating ~Rs 15.4M in domestic revenue. No significant external donor financing identified for the core MNIC system. Digital Mauritius 2030 strategy is funded domestically.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Both fingerprints and facial/iris data are collected. The MNIC system collects fingerprint minutiae (stored on card only, not in central DB following 2015 Supreme Court ruling) and high-resolution facial photographs. MNIC 3.0 launched in February 2024 collects biometric fingerprints and a facial image for card issuance. The National Identity Card Act (amended 2023) and NIC Regulations 2024 govern this.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Fully digital. The Central Population Database (CPD) holds all citizen records electronically and has been operational since 2013 (revamped in July/August 2023). The Civil Status Database is also being revamped and digitised. The National Identity Card Act (Section 3) mandates the register be kept in electronic form. No paper-only or mixed database systems are used for the core ID register.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Mauritius has a fully deployed nationwide digital ID system. The Mauritius National Identity Scheme (MNIS) has been operational since 2013 (MNIC 2.0) and was upgraded to MNIC 3.0 (launched February 2024). The Mobile ID (digital wallet version) was launched in September 2024 via the MWA app, making Mauritius the first African country to deploy a digital ID wallet meeting ISO standards. All citizens 18+ are legally required to hold a card under the National Identity Card Act (as amended 2023).

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The MNIC system is interoperable with other government systems via the InfoHighway platform, which connects 169 government agency connections (as of 2023). The Central Population Database (CPD), managed by the Civil Status Division, shares data with MRA, Ministry of Social Security, Bank of Mauritius (Central KYC), and other agencies. MauPass (launched 2020) uses CPD for citizen authentication across hundreds of e-services.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: NIC use for banking is mandatory (for Mauritian citizens). Banks require the NIC for customer onboarding KYC. MauBank explicitly states that during customer onboarding, Mauritian nationals must use their National Identity Card (passport cannot substitute). The Central KYC database (Bank of Mauritius/Civil Status Division/MTCI MOU) further entrenches mandatory NIC-based KYC for financial services. The NIC number is required for National Savings Fund contribution records.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The first issue of the National Identity Card is free of charge. The ID4Africa 2019 presentation by the Civil Status Division of Mauritius explicitly states: 'At the age of 18 or above: First issue-Free of Charge.' MNIC 3.0 cards for new applicants (age 18) are free; replacements/renewals reportedly cost Rs 350 (Rs 200 for pensioners). As the first issue (primary credential) is free, value=1 (No cost for initial credential).

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Some regional recognition. Mauritius is a COMESA member and has waived visas to all COMESA citizens. However, there is no formally interoperable digital ID cross-border arrangement. The Mobile ID was described as meeting ISO standards, and Mauritius participates in COMESA and SADC frameworks where national IDs may be accepted informally, but no formal mutual recognition treaty for the MNIC as a digital cross-border identity credential has been identified. Physical MNIC is accepted for COMESA visa-free travel on a bilateral basis.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Enrollment eligibility starts at age 18 (>17). The National Identity Card Act requires every Mauritian citizen to apply for an identity card within 6 months of attaining the age of 18. The NIC number is assigned at birth but the physical card is only issued from age 18. MNIC 3.0 launched in February 2024 applies to persons attaining the age of 18 and 60 (for renewals). MauPass (linked to the ID system) has a minimum age of 14 for registration but requires NIC which is only issued at 18.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Mandatory for all citizens. Section 4(1)(a) of the National Identity Card Act states: 'every person who is a citizen of Mauritius shall, within 6 months of attaining the age of 18... apply for an identity card.' Non-compliance is an offence. The Mobile ID (digital wallet version) is voluntary/optional as an addition. Only the physical NIC is mandatory.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: NIC is mandatory for free public healthcare access. Free medical care in Mauritius public hospitals is only available to NIC holders (citizens); non-citizens with residence permits pay for treatment. The MNIC 3.0 system was designed to potentially include health card functionality. The NIC is required to access social security-linked health benefits. Reddit community discussions and government sources confirm NIC as mandatory for free hospital treatment.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Non-nationals (non-citizens) are not eligible for the Mauritius National Identity Card. The NIC Act explicitly restricts eligibility to citizens of Mauritius. Non-citizens residing in Mauritius use passports/residence permits. For SIM registration and MauPass, non-citizens use passports and unique identification numbers (residence/occupation permits), not the NIC. There is no provision for refugee IDs or non-citizen national IDs.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Coverage exceeds 89% of the eligible population (citizens aged 18+). By June 2019, 1,666,808 Smart National Identity Cards had been issued, and enrollment is mandatory for all citizens 18+. Total population is ~1.27M (2024). As virtually all adult citizens are legally required to hold a card and the system has been operational since 2013, coverage of the eligible (18+) population is effectively >89%. A mobile team serves bedridden/disabled citizens for registration.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: Independent security audits are legally mandated and in progress. Section 2C of the NIC Act (inserted by Finance Act 2023, in force 19 February 2024) requires the National Identity Card Unit to 'appoint an independent body to carry out, at such intervals as may be prescribed, an independent security audit of the MNIC System.' The government committed to the UN Human Rights Committee to conduct independent security audits of MNIC 3.0. The Prime Minister publicly announced this commitment at the February 2024 MNIC 3.0 launch.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: NIC is mandatory for SIM card registration. The ICTA (Registration of SIM) Regulations 2023 (effective 31 October 2023) mandate that all SIM holders register using their NIC (or passport for non-citizens). All existing SIM holders had to re-register by 30 April 2024. Operators (my.t, Emtel, Chili) verify NIC photo against the applicant's photograph. Failure to register leads to SIM deactivation.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: NIC is mandatory to access social services. The National Savings Fund uses the NIC number for contribution records. Basic Retirement Pension, Widow's Pension, Social Aid, and all Ministry of Social Security benefits require the NIC as a mandatory document. The Social Register of Mauritius uses NIC for beneficiary identification. National Housing Development Company requires NIC for housing scheme applications.
